items.description: A rough grey iron ingot from the cupola. The foundry's own heavy feedstock; what the casting floor does not keep goes down the ice road, stamped for the Office's schedule.
A cast iron plowshare and moldboard. Agricultural continuity: the glasshouse allotments and the Verge rows trade seed and stores for these.
A forty-kilo structural T-beam. The bone of the bunker's sky-layer armor frames and Block C's load-bearing repairs.
Forged ice anchors, counted by the bundle. Driven into the Cut to hold lane markers, mooring chains, and the boom. A charter obligation to the Cutters — the road dies without them.
A cast winch drum, chilled and machined at the flange. Heavy, hard, and owed in quotas to the road charter — the barge and Berth 9 both wind on these.
A lead-antimony brine-resistant pipe and valve body, cast for the saltworks membrane hall. The Brine Pipe Exchange trades these for iodine.
A bolted repair plate for bunker bulkheads, blast doors, and the sky-layer armor grid. Shelter resilience in a flat rectangle of iron.
Cast brackets and threaded fasteners. The quiet hardware that holds piping, shelving, and machinery to the walls.
A cast valve body for the water system — brine, feedwater, and the outfall lines. The saltworks runs on these.
A heavy wrench, drift, or sledging bar from the foundry floor. Improves repair and maintenance work across the shelter.
A precision heavy-alloy part — a bearing sleeve, a gear blank, a tuyere boss. The most expensive thing the foundry makes, and the one nobody has spare.
A thickened armor plate for the blast doors and hatch surrounds. Defensive only where the structure demands it; the foundry does not run a weapons line.
Clay-bonded casting sand, wetted and sieved. The mold bed is the foundry's second furnace: it decides whether a casting is clean or cracked.
High-alumina firebrick for the lining and hearth. Scarce, and the difference between a furnace that holds iron and a furnace that kills people.
Crushed limestone flux. It pulls sulfur and slag out of the melt — without it, the iron is brittle and the air is poison.
A bag of lead-antimony shot for the brine-resistant alloy. The Office released the antimony from the naval yard's stores under the Brine Pipe Exchange; the iodine flows because these pipes hold.
Thickened sky-layer armor plate designed to withstand falling structural debris and acid rain fallout.
A heavy cast collar for shoring up deep excavation tunnels, sumps, and salt mine shafts.
Precision alloy bushing and hinge bracket for airlock blast doors and pressure bulkheads.
An anchored structural support shoe to stabilize subsiding foundation columns in lower blocks.
A cast iron coupling sleeve connecting heavy power conduits and steam lines across bunker sectors.
High-carbon alloy drop-stamping and forming die set used to rebuild workshop machine tools.
Hexagonal tool steel blanks for re-tipping rock drills and salt-mine augers.
Refractory-lined outer shell for foundry cupolas and smelter relining.
Precision high-pressure hydraulic collar for pharma tablet compactors and workshop presses.
Split-pillow block bearing housing for ventilation blower shafts and turbine rotors.
High-heat cast iron grate segment for shelter heating fireboxes and coal boilers.
Abstract aerodynamic shell body cast for atmospheric aerosol dispersion and fallout mitigation.
Chilled lead-iron defensive shot canister used in automated bunker deadfall traps and perimeter barriers.
Drawn alloy blank cups for high-value Garrison barter and armament treaty quotas.
